\section*{Question 6}

Consider the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=(3-y) \cos x\). Let \(y=f(x)\) be the particular solution to the differential equation with the initial condition \(f(0)=1\). The function \(f\) is defined for all real numbers.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] A portion of the slope field of the differential equation is given below. Sketch the solution curve through the point (0, 1).
\item[(b)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the solution curve in part (a) at the point (0, 1). Use the equation to approximate \(f(0.2)\).
\item[(c)] Find \(y=f(x)\), the particular solution to the differential equation with the initial condition \(f(0)=1\).
\item[(a)]
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/81d14fa1-b948-4490-827e-46897257bdbe-1.jpg?height=722&width=735&top_left_y=937&top_left_x=249)
\item[(b)] \(\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(x, y)=(0,1)}=2 \cos 0=2\)
An equation for the tangent line is \(y=2 x+1\).
\[
f(0.2) \approx 2(0.2)+1=1.4
\]
\item[(c)] \(\frac{d y}{d x}=(3-y) \cos x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{d y}{3-y}=\int \cos x d x \\
& -\ln |3-y|=\sin x+C \\
& -\ln 2=\sin 0+C \Rightarrow C=-\ln 2 \\
& -\ln |3-y|=\sin x-\ln 2
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(y(0)=1, y<3\), so \(|3-y|=3-y\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& 3-y=2 e^{-\sin x} \\
& y=3-2 e^{-\sin x}
\end{aligned}
\]
Note: this solution is valid for all real numbers.
\end{itemize}

1 : solution curve
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { tangent line equation } \\ 1: \text { approximation }\end{array}\right.\)
\(6:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { separation of variables } \\ 2: \text { antiderivatives } \\ 1: \text { constant of integration } \\ 1: \text { uses initial condition } \\ 1: \text { solves for } y\end{array}\right.\)
